messages:
Harper: Thinking out loud — proposal for a "session-lease" based gradual switchover + escape-hatch flow for A/B-type experiments. Goal: keep routing logic simple in the router and push complexity into a tiny handshake and TTL token so we can do fast, reversible swaps with minimal global state.

Liam: sketch it? short bullets pls, then we can iterate.

Harper: Sure. core idea: when we want to move traffic from variant=stable -> variant=new, we issue short-lived session leases (header: X-Session-Lease) that pin traffic for the lifetime of the TTL to the chosen variant. Traffic controller has three modes: probe, ramp, handoff.

Sophia: how is this different from affinity cookie we already have?

Harper: two differences: 1) leases are opaque low-entropy tokens signed by control plane and include variant+expiry. Router only verifies signature and TTL, no lookup. 2) escape-hatch: at any time control plane can mark a token family as "evict". routers will then treat those leases as expired and route to fallback. That avoids a centralized revocation lookup.

Ryan: sounds good. Concern: cache/kV warming — if we pin a user to new variant but new VM hasn't warmed KV cache, tail latency spikes. Any mitigation?

Harper: two mitigations: a) controlled warmup probe path — small percentage of requests to new variant bypass lease for warm probes (configurable), b) lease with a warmup-phase flag that tells router to do dual-write of metrics (so we can observe async warming).

Ana: can we see the header format? and example router logic?

Harper: example header / token: 
```
X-Session-Lease: s=eyJ2IjoiYWRkIiwiZXhwIjoxNjA5MjM0NTYwfQ==.sig
// decodes -> {"v":"add","exp":1709120000}  (base64 + HMAC)
```
router pseudo: 
```
if header present and signature valid and now < exp:
  route -> variant from token
else if control-plane forced-evict(token.family):
  route -> fallback_variant
else:
  follow normal allocation/policy
```

Mike: forced-evict(token.family) is the sticky part if we avoid a lookup. How do we mark family without lookups?

Harper: good call. two cheap options: 1) family id can be derived from token sig prefix and we publish a compact bloom filter/allowlist per router (push periodically), or 2) use a signed revocation counter in system state included in token payload: token contains epoch=E, control plane increments global epoch when marking evict, router compares token. That requires synced epoch but avoids per-token lookups.

Sophia: epoch approach is interesting. risk: clock/epoch skew causing valid tokens to be treated as revoked or vice versa. we should be conservative: router treats token as valid if token.epoch >= local_epoch - 1 (tolerate one epoch lag).

Liam: what about partial rollbacks? e.g., we want to move users with lease->new for 20% but instantly pull back to stable for 5% if error spike. How to express both gate and escape?

Harper: propose this control-plane state machine: 
- issue leases with variant=new and epoch=E, TTL=30m, percent=20
- monitor metrics; if error_spike then increment epoch->E+1 and set policy: evict_family(E) -> true and optionally route-injected fallback for a short period. routers see epoch mismatch and treat E leases as expired.

Ryan: operators want a manual "drain-to-old" option where new requests stop going to new variant but existing leases continue until expiry. We need both instant-evict and drain modes.

Harper: yep. control plane flags: {evict_mode: [instant | drain]}. instant -> bump epoch. drain -> stop issuing new leases and set percent=0 but don't bump epoch.

Ana: how is this surfaced to console? UX should show how many active leases exist, estimated time to fully drain (based on TTL distribution). Also show effect of instant-evict in real time.

Mike: implementation concerns: router needs only HMAC verification and epoch compare + small periodic state pushes (local_epoch). Push interval 1s-5s probably fine. Also rolling restarts shouldn't break behaviour if we persist local_epoch in memory.

Harper: tradeoffs: 
- Pros: no per-request lookup, reversible quickly, simple router checks.
- Cons: requires token signing, epoch sync, lease TTL management, operators must understand delay to drain.

Sophia: tests? propose we add an integration test harness: 
- synthetic traffic with mix of cold/warm users
- inject errors on new variant -> ensure instant-evict removes >99% traffic within 2s after epoch bump. (we may need to tune push interval)
- drain mode -> ensure traffic decays only as leases expire

Liam: what about metrics tagging and billing? are we double-counting requests if probes bypass token? should mark probe headers e.g. X-Lease-Probe: 1

Harper: yep. include X-Lease-Probe and X-Lease-Warmup to separate from billable traffic. console will subtract those from cost view.

deploy-bot: Note: scheduled deploy window at 2024-03-05 02:00 UTC. recommend feature flag gating until we have integration tests. :robot_face:

Harper: Agreed. next steps: I'll write a short RFC with enum config examples (instant/drain/percent), token schema (HMAC + epoch + variant), router pseudo patch, and a test plan. Anyone want to co-author?

Liam: I'll help with test harness and SRE scenarios.

Sophia: I'll review token schema and threat model (replay, forgery).

Ryan: ops playbook entries from me for "instant-evict" and monitoring runbooks.

Ana: I'll wire console views and TTL estimation.

Harper: awesome. I'll post RFC draft tomorrow and link here. Thanks for quick feedback :thumbsup:
